title: Division by Zero
concept: Prevent division by zero with requires: divisor != 0 — the canonical example of why contracts exist.
why: Division by zero crashes programs or produces NaN. Contracts catch the bad input BEFORE the division happens, with a clear error message.
tips: Don't just check for zero in the body — put it in requires so callers see the requirement
For Float64, consider requires: b.abs() > 0.0001 to also catch near-zero values
Modulo (%) also needs the zero check — it's the same hardware division operation
common_mistakes: Checking b != 0 in the body but not in requires — callers can't see the requirement
Forgetting to check for zero in recursive functions where the divisor is computed
Using || when you mean &&: requires: a != 0 || b != 0 allows ONE zero, not both
